fact: Data Center Dynamics (2026-08-19) says ACE, launched in 2012, lands at Conakry and is Guinea's only cable in service until Medusa becomes the second.
GUILAB's director general said on 2026-06-17 that Guinea has had a single submarine cable for nearly fifteen years, now saturated (cable not named in this document).
GUILAB's director general said on 2026-05-06 that ACE, the first cable which arrived nearly 13 years ago, is Guinea's only submarine cable and nearing critical load.
GUILAB's director general said on 2025-07-10 that Guinea has had one cable for over a decade, which carries about 54% of connectivity (cable not named).

The Medusa Submarine Cable System's announcement of 6 May 2026 describes the planned Medusa cable as Guinea's second submarine cable 'after ACE cable', so ACE is the one existing route; the landing station is not named for ACE.
The ACE consortium states the 17,000 km ACE cable has landed at Conakry, Guinea, as the first international submarine cable to land in Guinea, in service since 15 December 2012.

Ecofin Agency reports that GUILAB (La Guineenne de Large Bande) operates and maintains the Africa Coast to Europe (ACE) submarine cable landing station in Guinea and manages Guinea's capacity on ACE, ISO 9001:2015 certified since 22 December 2016.
Techpoint Africa says the country is connected to the ACE submarine cable, the first to land there.
Developing Telecoms says Guinea has a single international subsea link, ACE.
ECOWAS says the six countries of the Amilcar Cabral project currently have only one landing station.
The ministry's Secretary General told MPs on 27 October 2026 that Guinea depends on a single submarine cable as its only link, at end of life and at risk of saturation.
